fixtures.label: Every open receivable, aged by due date
fixtures.description: The PRIMARY document — the whole receivable book on the route's default anchor (`due_date`, the one the live Xero tenant ages by), and the only fixture whose Account column spans UNRELATED customers. Captured 2026-09-08 over all 28 open receivables, grouping to 14 accounts. Three jobs. (1) THE UNTRIMMED CHAIN. `statement.eta` trims each line's chain against its own scope; this family prints the whole chain on every row, and an `all` run is where that matters most — no common prefix to trim against and no addressee to have already named it. Censused 2026-09-07 over all 318 prod orgs, the 29 department nodes carry 8 distinct names, 24 of them sharing `Locations`, `Office` and `Transpo`; on this very population two accounts are both a `Locations`, separated only by the levels a leaf segment discards. That is api-cloudrun#923. ⚠️ Do not expect the collision to be READABLE in the golden — `applyPii` masks each leaf independently, so the two render as different fake names. What this pins is that the chain is composed and printed at all. (2) THE `all` SCOPE LINE — `scope.kind === "all"` prints "Every open receivable" and `scope.name` is `""`, the arm neither sibling reaches. (3) A NOT-YET-DUE ROW — invoice 2386 is dated forward (due 2026-10-02 against an as-of of 2026-09-08), so it lands in `current` with a NEGATIVE days-overdue. That is the case behind one of the two defects only the rendered page caught: a right-aligned Days column ran into the Bucket beside it and printed `-17Current` as one number. ⚠️ On this population only `current` and `1-30` carry money, so 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ all read $0.00 — a fact about a book nobody has let age, not a dead column; `subtree-invoice-date` is what puts money in a third bucket. ⚠️ `buildAgingReport` refuses any as-of date but today's, so this capture is a fact about 2026-09-08 and a re-capture renders different money BY CONSTRUCTION, not by drift.

fixtures.label: Scoped to a subtree, aged by invoice date
fixtures.description: The only SCOPED run, the only "and N sub-accounts" sentence, and the only fixture on the `date` anchor — three arms `all-accounts` cannot reach. `organization-subtree` on Netflix Productions, LLC, the widest prod org family at 14 nodes (the same root behind the statement family's `balance-forward-subtree`), captured 2026-09-08. (1) THE SCOPE LINE'S OTHER ARM. `scope.kind === "organization"` prints `scope.name` and, because `uids.length` is 14, appends "and 13 sub-accounts" — the plural branch of a sentence that is singular at 2 and absent at 1. `nothing-outstanding` holds the absent arm. (2) THE ANCHOR, and it is not cosmetic. `anchorText` prints "Invoice date" here against "Due date" on both siblings, and the anchor CHANGES EVERY BUCKET on the page: measured on this same corpus, aging by `due_date` puts money only in `current` and `1-30`, while aging by `date` reaches 31-60 as well. So this is also the family's only fixture with a third populated bucket — two runs on one morning that disagree entirely and are both right, which is why the document states which it used. (3) A NARROW ACCOUNT COLUMN THAT STILL SPANS TWO ACCOUNTS — Big Red / Office and Big Red / Locations, so the untrimmed chain is exercised where the chains share a prefix, the case `statement.eta` would have trimmed away. ⚠️ Deliberately SMALL — 3 open invoices — so the anchor's effect is the only thing worth looking at in the diff; do not enrich it. ⚠️ `buildAgingReport` refuses any as-of date but today's, so this is a fact about 2026-09-08 and a re-capture renders different money BY CONSTRUCTION, not by drift.
